findings.finding: The initial Canonical.lean snapshot omitted the ordered atom inventory from both contextual formulas and certified merges despite the revised contract requiring it. Equal fixed-index formulas alone did not distinguish independently atomized Alloy atoms.
findings.concrete_failure_scenario: Within one module, P=some A and Q=some B can each become Formula.atom 0 with n=1. Their Boolean tables agree although an Alloy instance with A nonempty and B empty distinguishes them. A certificate refl over the independently numbered bodies must not authorize a merge.
findings.remediation: Require explicit ordered inventory identity in canonicalKey and CertifiedMerge, with an F18 theorem and distinct some A/some B negative fixture.
findings.resolution_evidence: Reviewed patched source includes inventory : Fin n -> String, equality of inventory in CertifiedMerge, inventory in canonicalKey, distinct_inventories_distinct_keys, and a some A/some B negative example. Clean independent build passed.

findings.finding: Generated.lean, contract_has_witness and the regeneration/finite-closure artifacts were not yet available in the reviewed snapshot. This is an unfinished delivery check, not a failed theorem. A passing aggregate build currently covers only the modules actually imported.
findings.concrete_failure_scenario: A final report could cite a successful lake build while omitting a registered theorem or while the generated kernel differs from the frozen JSON configuration. This would overstate G0 completion even when every imported theorem is correct.
findings.remediation: Generate the exact formal-kernel projection, import it in the aggregate, check F15 and its axioms, verify regeneration byte equality and theorem coverage, then run the required isolated final builds against the frozen hashes.
findings.blocks: No unresolved model-source blocker. Final closure evidence must independently satisfy its registered checks.
findings.resolution_evidence: Final snapshot contains Generated.lean, Kernel.lean, Contract.lean and aggregate import. F15 compiles and #print axioms reports no axioms. All 19 registered obligation symbols resolve and compile. Deterministic generation --check passes against the final frozen snapshot. Final closure runner/report remains separate from this reviewer validation.

findings.finding: The proofs establish structural identities and policy implications over supplied tokens/flags. They do not establish that atom inventory strings encode Alloy syntax injectively, that polarity/formulaHash corresponds to F-and-P or F-and-not-P, or that a validated witness flag follows actual validation. The contract correctly identifies these semantic links as trusted and leaves implementation refinement to later gates.
findings.concrete_failure_scenario: A future adapter can attach negative polarity to F-and-P or mark arbitrary tuples validated; admitPair can then return true while all Lean policy theorems remain true. Similarly an adapter that erases binding identity before constructing an inventory can pass structural key equality.
findings.remediation: Keep these limitations in every assurance report. At G3/G4 require adversarial adapter checks for exact atom/binding identity, authenticated facts/context, generated query polarity and full-instance validation. No model theorem alone authorizes a product correctness badge.
findings.blocks: Nothing in the present specification/proof-only phase; these are existing G3/G4 obligations.

positive_findings: The contract preserves the explicit prohibition on product implementation in this phase.
No proof is inherited from ACGN or AlloyStudio and no Java, React, parser, solver or SQL refinement is claimed.
Accepted source/artifact revisions are separated from invalid drafts and monotone presentation epochs, preventing old accepted-state badges from silently endorsing an edited draft in the model.
Canonical table completeness is explicitly fixed-inventory Boolean completeness, with relational valuations and the 8-atom profile separated from general Alloy equivalence.
Positive and negative pools share target context while keeping separate query identities and checked polarity; empty pools, vector similarity and inconclusive statuses confer no solver authority.
Purpose-specific rights, withdrawal, deletion, tenant filtering and disabled remote/RAG/training features address the principal semantic risks of a future corpus.
Commercial status is explicitly uncleared; demand is a hypothesis, pilot thresholds must precede recruitment, and licenses/support economics remain measured release gates.

commercial_assessment.conclusion: Plausible narrowly scoped local/customer-managed Alloy workbench; no evidence yet establishes paid demand, installer feasibility, support economics or redistribution clearance. Requiring PostgreSQL/pgvector and limiting complete canonical profiles to 8 opaque atoms are concrete adoption/scope assumptions to validate in G5/G6.
commercial_assessment.recommendation: Use the predeclared pilot rule and measured installation/support cost before any commercial readiness claim.

suggestions.finding: Duplicate claim IDs collapse in set comparison; a duplicated claim can reach VERIFIED while total exceeds passed. Claim statement/verifier/predicate semantics are not bound to actual dispatched checks.
suggestions.remediation: Reject duplicate IDs; require exact expected claim inventory and per-claim semantic/verifier binding.

suggestions.finding: Provenance subset checks allow empty inputs and trust sets and ignore public_claim/evidence fields. A missing public target or nonexistent evidence path can pass.
suggestions.remediation: Validate exact evidence paths, public target binding, mandatory input/trust dependencies and unique complete public-claim coverage.

suggestions.finding: The manifest only checks listed files. It does not require coverage of every consumed authoritative input; omitted claims, config, registry, provenance, reviews or verifier inputs can change without root mutation.
suggestions.remediation: Define and enforce exhaustive normalized manifest coverage, explicitly resolving config input_root_hash self-reference; reject paths outside the root and any unmanifested verification inputs.

suggestions.finding: C25 tests whether current contract hash appears anywhere in the report JSON, rather than binding to an exact final review field and seat identity.
suggestions.remediation: Check exact final_review.contract_sha256 and unique matching reviewer identity; preserve actual model runtime identity as unattested.

suggestions.finding: Theorem audits #check and #print axioms verify symbol existence but do not bind required proposition types. An unrelated Nat-valued def with the same name can pass these checks.
suggestions.remediation: Freeze expected Lean proposition types and compile proof applications of every obligation/witness against its expected type, or use a trusted structural declaration/type extractor.
